sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Origin**: Established under **Section 4** of the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (PCA) Act, 1960**.
• **Nodal Ministry**: Originally under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), it was transferred to the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying** in 2018.
• **Headquarters**: Shifted from Chennai to **Ballabhgarh, Haryana**.
• **Mandate**: To advise the Government of India on animal welfare laws, grant recognition to animal welfare organizations, and provide financial assistance.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: 28 members, including MPs, representatives of animal welfare organizations, and government officials.
Prelims: Compositional balance is often a source of 'Incorrect Statement' questions.
Advising on PCA Act, rules, and regulations; monitoring animal shelters; promoting animal welfare education.
Mains: Critical for questions on 'Animal Rights vs. Development'.

items.definition: The primary legislation governing animal welfare in India. It defines 'animal' and 'cruelty' and provides the legal basis for the AWBI.
NGOs recognized by the AWBI to receive grants and implement welfare schemes at the grassroots level.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Animal Birth Control (ABC) Rules**: AWBI oversees the implementation of ABC programs to manage stray dog populations humanely.
• **Grant-in-Aid**: Financial support provided to AWOs for shelter maintenance and animal rescue.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of enforcement power (it is primarily advisory), limited funding, and conflict between traditional practices (e.g., Jallikattu) and animal rights.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the PCA Act, increasing state-level coordination, and integrating animal welfare into the 'One Health' framework.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-A-H-A' (Fisheries, Advisory, Haryana, Act 1960).
• **Decoded Meaning**: F (Fisheries Ministry), A (Advisory body), H (Haryana HQ), A (Act 1960).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states AWBI is a 'Constitutional Body' or 'Regulatory Body with enforcement powers'. It is a STATUTORY ADVISORY body.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Compassionate Governance' when discussing the role of AWBI in the context of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).

keyTakeaways: AWBI is a statutory body under the PCA Act, 1960, not the Constitution.
It is currently under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
Its primary role is advisory; it does not have direct police-like enforcement powers.
